To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the perturbation expansion in the propagator is finite and computationally tractable, 2) the propagator can be expressed as the sum of a discrete set of terms, each of which is a product of factors associated with branching points of 2d surfaces embedded in 4d, 3) the value of each branching point is determined by the hamiltonian matrix elements, 4) the sum of terms is invariant under 4d difeomorphisms,

the sum over surfaces form of loop quantum general relativity is a finite, computable and well-defined theory; the branching points play the roles of elementary vertices; the value of the branching point is determined by the known matrix element of the hamiltonia constraint; the theory can be viewed as an Ooguri-Craine-Yetter type topological quantum field theory with a new crossing symmetry related to diffeomorphism.

the perturbation series for the quantum propagator in loop quantum gravity is finite and computationally tractable, and that the perturbation theory can be expressed in a ``sum over surfaces'' form, with the surfaces being branched, colored, and 2d.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have derived a spacetime formulation that makes the relation of loop quantum gravity to TQFT manifest, and that we have proposed a new term in the hamiltonian that may be necessary to implement diffeomorphism covariance.
we are able to derive a finite perturbation theory for the evolution operator in LQG, and that we are able find a ``sum over surfaces'' representation for it.
, by combining loop quantum gravity and spin foam models, we have obtained a finite, well-defined, and non-trivial theory of quantum general relavity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
loop quantum gravity is not a perturbation theory of general relativity, but rather an exact formulation of quantum gravity that is finite and computationally tractable.
loop quantum gravity, when formulated as a perturbative quantum field theory, is finite and computationally manageable.
the perturbation series of the theory is well-defined and computable, and can be given a simple graphical representation.
